title: Southern California Wildfires: Six Months of Unprecedented Recovery - 1080p
description:
U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Recovery Field Office Commander Col. Eric Swenson provides a look at the past six months of collaboration and debris removal effort in the Eaton and Palisades fire impact area.

(U.S. Army Corps of Engineers video by Charles Delano)
keywords: DEBRIS REMOVAL, USACE, Emergency Response, Southern California Wildfires 2025
unit_name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Los Angeles District

transcript.text: Hi , my name is Colonel Eric Swenson ,
Army Corps of Engineers , and I'm the
recovery Field Office commander . The
fires in the Eaton fire impacted area
started on the 7th of January . I
arrived with my colleagues from the
Army Corps of Engineers starting on the
12th of January , and we quickly
partnered with local , state , and
federal government in order to figure
out a way to get all of this public
health and safety threats removed so
the community can rebuild , and it's
been a long journey over the past 6
months to get to this . When I first
got here , what we saw were thousands
of homes destroyed by a fire , families
who were impacted that evacuated the
night of the 7th or the morning of the
8th , oftentimes in the cover of
darkness , escaping to save their lives
and taking only their most valuable
possessions with them . When they
returned home a day or 2 or 3 days
later , what they found was their homes
had been impacted by this fire and
everything they had worked for was lost .
When we came in , we wanted to partner .
The local community and with these
survivors and provide them heart and
handshake to get these community back
on their feet . And over the past 6
months we have met these community
where they're at . We have worked with
them . We've helped them find lost
articles that they thought were lost to
the fire . We have found possessions
that might not have any material value
but had great value to the survivor who
thought they were lost . In the past 6
months , we have cleared over 95% of
Parcels in both the Eaton fire impacted
area and the Palisades fire impacted
area and that represents somewhere on
the order of 4 million tons of debris
have been removed from these
communities and safely transported on
highways to proper disposal sites . And
in the case of the recyclables , they
can get reused in the supply chain .
Behind me , what you see is the 6 month
effort of the Army Corps of Engineers
to remove the fire , ash and debris ,
that public health and safety threat
that At the core to this community to
help them recover from the devastating
wildfires that started on the 7th of
January . And today I'm pleased to
announce that we are almost done with
all the debris removal from this fire
in this community , and our efforts to
go fast , to go safely has enabled
residents like the one behind me to
start rebuilding their home . So the
recovery effort that's underway right
now has truly been a record setting
pace . I think nowhere else in modern
history has the core of or even the
state been able to recover and get the
debris removed this quickly after a
devastating wildfire , and we're proud
to be part of this and part of the
story of this community and helping
them get themselves back onto their
feet . But on behalf of the federal
government , it's an honor to be here
to help this community recover and to
bring a federal benefit to those in
this community which is in need as they
are still recovering from the
devastating impacts of the fires that
struck this community on the 7th .
